Quranic quote: ﴿By the sky and the Tariq﴾ ... wait, I must keep markers and translate meaning.

**Translation:**

﴿By the heaven and the Night-Comer﴾. Its root meaning is everything that comes at night, and from this (comes the word) "the stars" (al-nujum), because of their appearing at night.

﴿And what will make you know what the night-comer is?﴾ made you know (أعْلَمك). ﴿What the night-comer is﴾ is a mubtada' (subject, مُبْتَدَأ) and khabar (predicate, خَبَر) construction, in the position of the second object (المَفْعُول الثّانِي) of لَأَدْرى (adrā, "to make know"). The ما that follows the first ما (الأُولى) is its khabar. In this there is a glorification of the status of the night-comer, which is explained by what follows it: it is
﴿The star﴾, i.e., the Pleiades (al-Thurayya), or every star. ﴿The piercing one﴾, the bright one that pierces the darkness with its light. And the answer to the oath (jawab al-qasam)

Qur'an 86:4: "There is no soul but that it has over it a guardian."

Tafsir al-Jalalayn: "﴿Verily, every soul has over it a guardian﴾ With the lightening of 'in' (in), 'ma' is extra and 'in' is the lightened form of the heavy (inna), its noun being omitted, i.e. 'innahu' (indeed it), and the lam is the lam that distinguishes (lam al-fariqa). And with its doubling, 'in' is negative and 'lamma' means 'illa' (except). The guardian is from the angels, who guard its deeds, good and bad."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 86, verse 5:

﴿So let man look at what he was created from﴾ a look of reflection; ﴿from what he was created﴾, from what thing.

Qur'anic quotation: "He has been created from a gushing fluid."

This is the answer to His saying "From what is he created?" "He has been created from a gushing fluid" — that is, one that gushes forth, from the man and the woman into her womb.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 86, verse 7:

﴿It comes out from between the backbone﴾ of the man ﴿and the ribs﴾ of the woman, and they are the bones of the chest.

Indeed He (Exalted is He) is ﴿Able to return him﴾, that is, to resurrect the human being after his death. ﴿So when he considers his origin, he knows that the One Able to do that is Able to resurrect him.﴾

Translation:

﴿On the Day when secrets are tested﴾ — tested and laid bare — ﴿the hidden things﴾ — the inner thoughts of the hearts concerning beliefs and intentions.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 86, verse 10:

﴿So he will have no power﴾ for the one who denies the resurrection, ﴿by which he may defend himself against the punishment﴾ ﴿nor any helper﴾ who would repel it from him.
﴿By the sky which returns﴾: **al-raj'** (الرَّجْع), the rain, because it returns every time.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 86, verse 12:**

﴿By the earth which splits open﴾, meaning it splits open for the plants.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 86, verse 13:

﴿Indeed, it﴾ i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿is a decisive word﴾ that distinguishes between truth and falsehood.

Verse 86:14 is quoted: ﴿And it is not a jest﴾, and the commentary says: "not by play or falsehood."

Here is the translation of the passage:

﴿And it is not a jest﴾ — not by play and falsehood (بِاللَّعِبِ والباطِل).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 86, verse 15:

﴿Indeed they﴾ i.e., the disbelievers, ﴿are plotting a plot﴾, they devise schemes against the Prophet (ﷺ).
﴿And I plot a plot﴾ — I draw them on gradually from where they do not know.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 86, verse 17:

﴿So give respite﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿to the disbelievers; give them respite﴾. The repetition is a emphasis (ta'kid), made pleasing by the variation in wording, i.e., "allow them time" (anzirhum). ﴿Gradually﴾, meaning a little, and it is a verbal noun (masdar) emphasizing the meaning of the verb, diminutive of rawd or arwad, by elision (tarkhim). Allah the Exalted did seize them at Badr, and the respite was abrogated (naskh) by the verse of the sword, i.e., the command to fight (qital) and to strive (jihad).
